edges.effect_quant: Among 192 patients with non-transfusion-dependent thalassemia, serum ferritin and liver iron concentration were significantly elevated versus healthy controls, and in thalassemia intermedia ferritin levels around 916 to 940 ng/mL corresponded to liver iron concentration above 5 mg Fe/g dry weight.
edges.population: people with thalassemia trait or other non-transfusion-dependent thalassemia phenotypes
edges.mechanism: Thalassemia syndromes can suppress hepcidin and increase gastrointestinal iron absorption even without transfusions, creating a baseline tendency toward iron loading. In that context, empiric iron supplementation without proven deficiency can add to an already dysregulated iron pool and worsen tissue overload risk.
edges.summary: Routine iron supplementation is generally a poor fit for thalassemia minor unless true iron deficiency is documented, because thalassemic erythropoiesis itself can favor iron loading. The evidence tying supplementation specifically to overload in trait carriers is indirect, but the biologic rationale and related thalassemia data make the contraindication clinically sensible.
edges.caveats: This is a low-certainty edge because direct intervention trials of iron supplementation in beta-thalassemia minor are scarce. It should not be read as saying that every thalassemia trait carrier is iron overloaded, only that empiric iron should be avoided unless deficiency is demonstrated.
